land.text: 'In 1180 when the Duchy of Saxony ceased to exist' the rights over Paderborn passed to Cologne and the claims were settled in the 13th century, mostly in Paderborn's favour

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the lands inside Holy Roman Empire Minor States from 1260.

land.text: 'During the German Mediatisation in 1802, the bishopric became Prussian'

successors.note: From 1807 to 1813 part of the Kingdom of Westphalia (page); the diocese was recreated by Pius VII in 1821.

correction.text: the Hochstift Paderborn round Paderborn, a stand-in circle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Paderborn row). The page gives no area, no population and no district names (Warburg, Dringenberg, Delbrück and Büren are not mentioned); a 28 km circle at Paderborn (about 2,460 km2), soft.

ledger.note: 1281: the principality. 'In 1281, when only bishop-elect, he received the regalia from Rudolph of Habsburg'; the infobox gives the state as 1281 to 1802; after Worringen (1288) 'the bishops gained more sovereignty'. The diocese itself was founded in 799.
1802: 'During the German Mediatisation in 1802, the bishopric became Prussian' (infobox 1281 to 1802; the Final Recess is of February 1803 and the page gives no month).

wars.name: Soest Feud (Paderborn's part)
wars.outcome: 'During the feuds of the bishop with the city of Soest (1444-49) Paderborn was devastated.'
wars.note: The page names no land that changed hands; the Soest Feud is recorded in the electorate-of-cologne dossier.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary or area; the circle is a stand-in.

sources.title: Prince-Bishopric of Paderborn

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 5, thin page). New state: Cliopatria has no Paderborn row.

SHAPE. A 28 km circle at Paderborn (8.75E 51.72N); the gazetteer has the place 'Paderborn' (population None). The page names no district and no acquisition.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Area, boundary and acquisitions. (2) Start: 1281 (infobox) against c. 1200 (bailiwick returned to the bishops) against 1180. (3) End: infobox 1802 against the Final Recess of 25 February 1803; the Münster dossier of this batch uses the 1802 Prussian occupation and the 1803 secularisation. (4) The page does not describe a Wittelsbach union with Cologne; Ferdinand of Bavaria (1618-50) and Clemens August (1719-61) are listed as also Elector of Cologne. (5) The Soest Feud (1444-1449) is the only war on the page.
